sources.cite: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1):S132-S149
sources.note: Relayed from the LPNVN case ltc-insulin-hypoglycemia, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary text, PMC12690178). Table 6.4: level 1 glucose <70 and >=54 mg/dL, level 2 <54 mg/dL, level 3 a severe event with altered mental and/or physical status requiring assistance. Rec 6.15: glucose is preferred for the conscious person with glucose <70 mg/dL; repeat the treatment 15 min after if hypoglycemia persists; text: 15 g carbohydrate for most people, recheck 15 min after. Rec 6.16 and text: glucagon for people unable or unwilling to take carbohydrate by mouth.

sources.cite: CDC. Treatment of Low Blood Sugar (Hypoglycemia) (last reviewed 2024-05-15)
sources.note: Relayed from the LPNVN case ltc-insulin-hypoglycemia, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary web page). The 15-15 rule: 15 g of carbs, wait 15 min, recheck, repeat if still below 70 mg/dL; 15 g is 4 ounces (half a cup) of juice or 3-4 glucose tablets; foods high in fat such as chocolate slow sugar absorption; afterwards eat a balanced snack or meal with protein and carbs; oral sugar only for someone awake and able to swallow.

sources.cite: Lupin Pharmaceuticals. Glucagon for Injection, prescribing information (revised March 2024)
sources.note: Relayed from the LPNVN case ltc-insulin-hypoglycemia, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary PDF). Adults: 1 mg subcutaneously or intramuscularly; a second dose may be given while waiting for emergency help if no response after 15 min; turn the person on their side (they may vomit on waking); give oral carbohydrate once they respond and can swallow. Section 12.2: glucose rises within 10 min of a subcutaneous dose; after an intramuscular dose the mean peak glucose was 138 mg/dL at 26 min.

sources.cite: Lilly Medical. What are the pharmacodynamic properties of Humulin and Humalog (insulin lispro)?
sources.note: Relayed from the LPNVN case ltc-insulin-hypoglycemia, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary web page). Subcutaneous insulin lispro: more rapid onset than regular human insulin; time to peak insulin concentration 30 to 90 min; shorter duration than regular human insulin (no number given); properties vary between and within people.
